newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GOVERNMENT LIKELY TO PASS BANKING LAW TUE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GOVERNMENT LIKELY TO PASS BANKING LAW TUE.

text.p: The Polish government is likely to discuss and pass amendments to the banking law and banking guarantee fund (BFG) bills, the government spokeswoman said.

"Probably tomorrow the council of ministers will approve the proposed amendments to those bills (on banking law and banking guarantee fund)," Aleksandra Jakubowska said during her weekly news conference.

The government put off the work on the bills earlier this month because the Supreme Audit Chamber (NIK) wanted to have greater access to confidential banking information than the finance ministry and the central bank wanted to accept.
Jakubowska said the government's legal experts agreed that the NIK should not have access through BFG files to confidential information which it was allowed to gain by controlling individual banks.
The long-awaited amendments to the banking law adjust regulations to new, more stringent safety requirements and aim at bringing the regulations closer to the European Union standards.
